notes: The service each Shopify preferredRateSelection pair names, for the requested-
selection rung. Keyed by the exact `carrier:service` string PolyBag sends,
which is also what ShopifyAdapter writes to metadata.shopify_requested_service_code.
This is the weakest rung and runs last. A selection is what was asked for, not
what was observed: the tracking number and the label are the artefact Shopify
produced, this is the request that produced it. It fills in only where both
of those decline -- a UPS service whose 1Z indicator is not yet tabled, a
carrier whose number encodes nothing -- and where a decode disagrees with the
selection the ladder reports the disagreement and picks neither.
A pair is evidence only when Shopify's own report of the carrier agrees with
the carrier the pair asked for. The rung compares the two before it reads
this table, so a selection Shopify did not honour resolves to nothing.
Service names are the same vocabulary the other tables use -- USPS's product
names as the Service Type Code appendix spells them, UPS names as CarrierSeeder
spells them -- so a decode and a selection for the same service compare equal.

provenance.source: issue shopify-shipping-carrier/02: preferredRateSelection is honoured, and each carrier's own vocabulary is passed through
observed_on: Honouring, established by purchase rather than assumed. A pair with no
matching rate fails synchronously with RATES_NOT_FOUND and buys nothing, so a
purchase that succeeded with a selection is one Shopify matched a rate to.
USPS: a production purchase with usps:PriorityExpress came back priced an
order of magnitude above what auto had chosen from the same inputs, and the
order timeline read back through Order.events named the service.
UPS: purchases with ups_shipping:65, :07, :08 and :11 returned 1Z numbers
whose service level indicators (04, 66, 67, 68) match the indicators a 3PL's
twenty-year production history holds for exactly those services -- an
independent record agreeing with what was asked for, on every international
The service each code names is the carrier's own published vocabulary: USPS
product names for the PascalCase codes, and UPS's numeric service codes,
the same alphabet CarrierSeeder's UPS block carries.
not_included: dhl_express:P (DHL Express Worldwide). The oracle matches a rate for it and
DHL's product code P is documented, but no purchase has been made with it,
so the selection has never been seen honoured. A DHL waybill encodes no
service, which makes this the pair where the rung would matter most -- add
it after one purchase, and record the order here.
